newsitem.title: USA: FOMC members see US economy differently - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: FOMC members see US economy differently - Greenspan.

text.p: The members of the Federal Open Market Committee maintain differing views on the fundamental state of the U.S. economy, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said Tuesday.
"There are differences within the FOMC, as there are differences within any committee," Greenspan said during his testimony before a House Banking subcommittee.
"There are no differences with respect to the ultimate goal of monetary policy," he added.
The Fed chief said that recent economic developments in the United States have not always followed the "normal experience" of the past decade, leading to some disagreement among FOMC members.
"While there is no question something different is happening, you cannot basically say that because something different is happening, therefore, all history is irrelevant," he said.
